fix.how: Present a coherent CPU policy: match vendor, brand, feature dependencies, cache and topology to the configured vCPUs and real model. Do not advertise instructions the guest cannot execute.
fix.chimera: Validate Xen CPUID policy together with cpuidmon -s. Host-derived SMBIOS does not change CPUID. Test both guests and every advertised CPU leaf after masking.

fix.how: Calibrate on comparable bare metal and minimize exits and host scheduling noise. TSC offsetting/scaling and exit-cost compensation require coordinated hypervisor work; a static offset cannot remove per-exit cost and clock compensation must remain consistent across vCPUs and clocks.
fix.chimera: Not fixable by configuration. cpuidmon -s rewrites CPUID values but turns every CPUID into a vm_event round trip to dom0 (about 35x the plain exit cost, see the G2 numbers); masking through the Xen CPUID policy instead (xl.cfg cpuid=, verify that Xen 4.19 honours clearing the bit for HVM) removes the monitor cost but not the ~2.5k-cycle exit. Hiding the exit itself needs Xen-side TSC compensation for CPUID exits, which Xen 4.19 does not have; tsc_mode, TSC scaling and vCPU pinning do not remove per-exit cost. CHIMERA G2 measurements (2026-10-29, i7-13700HX host): median RDTSC;CPUID;RDTSC 2398-3720 cycles on the Xen HVM guest without an introspection monitor and 92530-94514 cycles with DRAKVUF cpuidmon -s, which forwards every CPUID to the dom0 monitor; al-khaser's avg10 rule fired 1000/1000 in every configuration, dom0 included (1590-1964 cycles).
